# Aera

> Aera is a sleep and running tracker for iPhone and Apple Watch. It reads Apple Health, compares last night and the past week with your own usual range, and tells you each morning how hard to go today: rest day, go easy, good to go or go for it. Every number in the app opens a short article that shows how it was worked out and where it stops being reliable. There is no account, and health numbers are worked out and kept on the iPhone.

Facts, stated plainly:

- Platform: iPhone and Apple Watch (reads Apple Health). Made by one person, Gergő Varga.
- Price: free to download and free to use. Premium is optional (monthly, yearly with a 7-day trial, or a one-time purchase).
- Free: recovery, stress, strain and a sleep score; a hard, easy or rest call every morning; a route planner on real paths with turn-by-turn directions on iPhone or Apple Watch; every workout read and every personal best; Flyover replays of runs from the last seven days; twelve months of history; raw data export as JSON or GPX.
- Premium: today's session (how long and how hard), sleep reserve, places, Flyover for older runs, every drawn route kept, history past twelve months, reports and every export format.
- Privacy: no account, no sign-in, no language model in the app. Product analytics stay off until the user turns them on and never include health values.
- Without an Apple Watch, Aera works from what the iPhone records (steps, workouts); reads that need overnight watch data wait until there is data.
- Not a medical device. Watch measurements such as sleep stages are estimates.
- Languages: English, Hungarian, German, Spanish and French in full; Italian, Japanese, Portuguese and Traditional Chinese in part.

- [All guides](https://aerahealth.app/guides/): every guide in English, Hungarian and German
- [Apple Watch HRV normal range](https://aerahealth.app/guides/apple-watch-hrv-normal-range.html): why there is no single normal HRV, what Apple Watch measures (SDNN), why yours is low, and why your own range matters most
- [Apple Watch HRV érték](https://aerahealth.app/guides/apple-watch-hrv-ertek.html): the same guide in Hungarian
- [Apple Watch HRV Normalwert](https://aerahealth.app/guides/apple-watch-hrv-normalwert.html): the same guide in German
- [What is a good sleep score on Apple Watch?](https://aerahealth.app/guides/what-is-a-good-sleep-score.html): Apple's 0-100 Sleep Score bands, what moves the score, and how Aera's own sleep score differs
- [Apple Watch alváspontszám](https://aerahealth.app/guides/jo-alvas-pontszam.html): the same guide in Hungarian
- [Guter Schlafscore auf der Apple Watch](https://aerahealth.app/guides/guter-schlafscore.html): the same guide in German
- [Apple Watch sleep and training, no subscription needed](https://aerahealth.app/guides/apple-watch-sleep-and-training-without-a-subscription.html): what Apple Watch tracks on its own, what an app adds and costs (Aera is free to use, with optional Premium by month, year or a one-time Lifetime purchase), and when a dedicated strap suits better
- [Whoop Alternative für Apple Watch: kein Abo nötig](https://aerahealth.app/guides/whoop-alternative-apple-watch.html): the same guide in German
- [Zone 2 heart rate for running](https://aerahealth.app/guides/zone-2-heart-rate-running.html): four ways to find your own zone 2 range, running it with Apple Watch, why it feels slow, cardiac drift and the 80/20 research
- [Zóna 2 pulzus](https://aerahealth.app/guides/zona-2-pulzus-futas.html): the same guide in Hungarian
- [Zone 2 Puls berechnen](https://aerahealth.app/guides/zone-2-puls-laufen.html): the same guide in German
- [Apple Watch resting heart rate](https://aerahealth.app/guides/apple-watch-resting-heart-rate.html): what is normal, why runners read lower, what raises it and when to see a doctor
- [Nyugalmi pulzus normál érték](https://aerahealth.app/guides/nyugalmi-pulzus-apple-watch.html): the same guide in Hungarian
- [Ruhepuls und Apple Watch](https://aerahealth.app/guides/ruhepuls-apple-watch.html): the same guide in German
- [Apple Watch VO2 max](https://aerahealth.app/guides/apple-watch-vo2-max.html): how Cardio Fitness is estimated, how close it gets to a lab test, what is good for your age and how to raise it
- [VO2 max Apple Watch (magyar)](https://aerahealth.app/guides/vo2-max-apple-watch-pontossag.html): the same guide in Hungarian

- [Futás 3D visszajátszás iPhone-on](https://aerahealth.app/guides/futas-3d-visszajatszas.html): the 3D replay guide in Hungarian
- [Lauf in 3D abspielen](https://aerahealth.app/guides/lauf-in-3d-abspielen.html): the 3D replay guide in German
- [Should I run after a bad night's sleep?](https://aerahealth.app/guides/should-i-run-after-bad-sleep.html): what a short night, a raised resting heart rate and lower HRV against your own usual mean for today's run, with a rest, easy, normal or hard guide
- [Fussak ma, ha rosszul aludtam?](https://aerahealth.app/guides/fussak-ha-rosszul-aludtam.html): the same guide in Hungarian

- [How to plan a running route](https://aerahealth.app/guides/plan-a-running-route.html): distance from your door, out-and-back, loop or point-to-point, how hills change your time, surface, light and water, how to estimate how long it takes, and how to follow a route turn by turn on iPhone and Apple Watch (free in Aera, even with no signal)

- [Laufroute planen: so geht's](https://aerahealth.app/guides/laufroute-planen.html): the same guide in German
